text:
alice: onboarding note: trying neptune-64k-int3 in staging for long-context workloads. Quick smoke shows occasional token "shift" after repeated anchor phrases at ~20k tokens.

 tom: can you paste a tiny reproducer?

 alice: sure, minimal reproducer (python):
```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=\"staging\")
prefix = (\"Anchor phrase. \" * 4000) + \"THE END\"
resp = c.generate(model=\"neptune-64k-int3\", prompt=prefix, max_tokens=64)
print(resp.text[:200])
```

 zhen: interesting. Is the pattern deterministic across runs or flaky?

 alice: deterministic on my machine: two runs produce different tail tokens starting at token ~20021. The divergence persists if I re-run same seed.

 riley: what about fp16 baseline? and int4?

 alice: fp16: clean up to 60k. int4: divergence shows earlier at ~18k. int3 shows at ~12k in some prompts, but when prompt has many repeated short phrases it surfaces at ~20k. int8 seems fine.

 cache-bot: KV-CACHE: active_prefill_mode=buffered, eviction_boundary=16384, prefill_target=24576, last_prefill_span=20000

 tom: buffered prefill + eviction_boundary mismatch could leave partial KV windows that shift absolute token index mapping. we've seen similar with other models but not at 64k.

 zhen: could also be RoPE wrap/aliasing interacting with quant noise. If rotary phase uses int3-friendly quant tables it might underflow phase precision at large indices.

 infra-bot: KERNEL-SELECTOR: chosen_kernel=quant-fused-remat-v2, fallback_kernel=quant-simple, device=rtx-a6000, driver=536.40

 riley: kernel selection log is important. fused-remat sometimes reorders matmuls for memory vs precision tradeoffs.

 alice: I tried toggling kernel to quant-simple by forcing runtime flag --quant-kernel=quant-simple and reran. divergence still present but shifted by +2 tokens.

 tom: good signal that both kernel and cache interplay. can you capture KV offsets and rot-phase snapshots? we need to compare expected kv-index -> position map.

 alice: uploaded artifacts to BUG-2563: https://tracker.redwood/BUG-2563 (includes dump: kv_offsets.bin, rot_phase.npy, model-selection.log, reproducer).

 zhen: schedule small eval: run 50-item goldset across neptune-64k-int3, neptune-48k-fp16, and neptune-64k-int8. track mismatch rate, perplexity, and tail token exact-match at positions 18k-22k.

 riley: +1 also track latency percentiles and kernel-run counts. If int3 triggers fused kernel more often, correlation might appear.

 alice: kicked off eval job job_id=1725252700. linking telemetry dashboard: https://dash.redwood/jobs/1725252700

 cache-bot: SUGGESTION: set active_prefill_mode=atomic to avoid partial window writes. Toggle reduces prefill_target to eviction_boundary when enabled.

 tom: atomic prefills are safer but costlier (higher latency and memory pressure). for canary we can try atomic on a small percentage of traffic.

 zhen: if atomic fixes correctness, we should also add a regression test that inserts repeated anchors at scale and asserts kv-index parity between quantized and fp16 paths.

 alice: agreed. I'll run atomic-prefill A/B with 10% of canary traffic and monitor mismatch_count metric.

 riley: FYI add a tiny synthetic test in model-onboard CI that primes a 30k repeating anchor sequence and diffs outputs across quant kernels. that will catch regressions earlier.

 alice: noted. will update BUG-2563 with test plan and schedule. thanks all. :party_popper:
